lifecycle.headline: BROKEN DOWN FOR PARTS
lifecycle.body: This deck no longer exists physically — its cards were pulled and sleeved into another list. Everything below was true when it shipped and is kept as published; the decklist is no longer maintained.

todo.what: the captain's log — `deck-notes add`; debriefed by the `debrief` agent
todo.how: manamap pilot deck-notes yawgmoth-swarm add "<what happened>" --result win|loss --opponents 3

notes: MONO-BLACK, built pool-only from share/ (764 owned cards). Every maindeck card is owned. Nothing in the 100 is a purchase.
PRIMARY KILL (✓ rules-verified, stack 001, checker pass, 3 iterations): Blowfly Infestation + Nest of Scarabs is an unbounded loop. 38 completed iterations take four opponents from 40 to 0.

BASTION OF REMEMBRANCE IS A HARD REQUIREMENT, NOT A FLEX SLOT. Stack 001 proved the build requirement is a body count. Blowfly's target locks when its trigger is put on the stack (CR 115.1d), at which moment state-based actions have already killed the counter-bearing token (CR 117.5) and Nest's replacement Insect does not yet exist. Whatever creature is on the battlefield at that instant is what Blowfly eats. A CREATURE drain (Zulaport Cutthroat) therefore needs three creatures on board at loop start — the drain, the counter-bearer, and one spare — or it is forcibly eaten on iteration one and the drain stops at 3 per opponent, ending them at 37 with no finite number of iterations reaching zero. Bastion is an Enchantment, so Blowfly can never target it, AND its enters-the-battlefield trigger supplies the 1/1 Human Soldier that absorbs the ignition counter. It satisfies both halves alone.

Zulaport Cutthroat and Blood Artist are kept as redundancy, not as the primary drain. Both strategy agents originally named Zulaport as the pod kill on correct arithmetic (it drains EACH opponent) and were wrong about the board.

SECOND KILL, one purchase away: Exquisite Blood (PURCHASE) pairs with the already-owned, otherwise-idle Enduring Tenacity for a two-card infinite. Enduring Tenacity is pinned above for that reason. UNVERIFIED — no resolve-stack run yet.

The 35 pins exist because the deterministic scorer weights similarity 0.30 and synergy 0.22 against EDHREC 0.10, so it optimises for on-theme rather than powerful. Left to itself on the previous build it passed over Necropotence, Vampiric Tutor and Lightning Greaves in favour of bulk. The pins are the correction.

TIER 2 — PURCHASES, NOT OWNED, and deliberately NOT in the 100. They live in the Considering section of decklist.txt so they are visible without ever being counted as maindeck: Exquisite Blood, Mikaeus the Unhallowed, Reassembling Skeleton, Gravecrawler, Ophiomancer, Bloodghast, Grave Pact, Dictate of Erebos, Imp's Mischief, Cabal Coffers, Phyrexian Altar. (Mana Crypt was on this list and was removed — cards.csv records it legal_commander=banned.)
DO NOT BUY, verified against oracle text: Cursed Totem turns off the commander's own activated ability. Grafdigger's Cage blanks the deck's own recursion. Exhume is symmetric across four opponents.

value: Simulates resource development, not full games (no interaction, no removal).
Draw every turn including turn 1 (multiplayer Commander).
Mulligan: keep 7-card hands with 2-5 lands; up to 2 fresh redraws, keep the last.
One land drop per turn when available.

LANDS ENTER UNTAPPED, ALWAYS, and the one in hand longest is the one played. A tapland costs nothing here and no land is ever chosen over another, so this model CANNOT rank two lands that make the same colours — `mana-analysis` and `mana-fit` are what answer a land question, and they are deterministic for exactly this reason.
Mana rocks ('{T}: Add') contribute from the turn after they are cast.
Commander cast on first affordable turn (highest spending priority).
Bodies count = creatures cast + tokens parsed from 'create ... token' text.
Target assembly counts cards DRAWN by a turn (cast cards still count).

CARD DRAW IS ONE A TURN UNLESS `model_draw` IS SET. With the flag on, four channels are modelled — a card's own ETB draw, an instant or sorcery that draws, an upkeep trigger, and an ARRIVAL trigger that draws when other creatures or tokens enter (Welcoming Vampire, Caretaker's Talent), which rides the same single door the ETB damage payoffs use. Activated draw (needs a spending policy this model has no opinion on), X-based draw (board-dependent), and death- or attack-triggered draw (no deaths, and attacks only under `model_combat`) are NOT modelled and the cards are named in `meta.card_advantage.draw_not_modelled`. A conditional trigger — 'if you control an artifact', 'you may draw' — is treated as unmodelled rather than assumed to be on: 39 of the 348 ETB-draw cards in the corpus carry one.

AN ARRIVAL-DRAW ENGINE NEVER SEES ITS OWN ARRIVAL. Welcoming Vampire is a 2/3 that draws 'whenever one or more OTHER creatures you control with power 2 or less enter'; registered before its own entry it passed its own gate and drew a card it does not draw, overstating edgar-vampires by 22% at turn eight. The deferral applies to every card and not only the ones worded 'other', which understates Tocasia's Welcome and two relatives by one draw on the turn they land.

ARRIVAL DRAW IS SMALLER WITHOUT `model_combat`, and legitimately so. The channel rides the one door onto the battlefield, which `model_combat` also uses to spawn token copies and ETB-payoff tokens — those are real additional arrivals that do not exist in the resource-only model. Measured on edgar-vampires: 1.264 extra cards by turn ten with both flags against 1.106 with draw alone. Before 2026-08-28 the gap was 1.264 against 0.323, because every call to that door sat inside `if model_combat:` and a draw-only deck silently lost three quarters of its arrival draws.

HELD-UP INTERACTION is reported as two series and both are FLOORS. This model casts everything it can afford every turn, so `interaction_castable` is what a pilot developing at full speed has left over, not what a pilot choosing to hold up two mana would have. A low figure is therefore a real finding and a high one is unambiguous good news.

Tutors are modeled as wildcards: a CAST tutor that fetches to hand or the top — including a TYPED one (Worldly Tutor, Sarkhan's Triumph), which the old literal 'a card' match missed entirely — fills ONE missing any_of group. Consumed once, mana paid, and a tutor that puts the card on top of the library costs a turn. An ACTIVATED, ETB or death-triggered tutor does not count, because this model only knows 'drawn and affordable'; nor does a land fetch, which is ramp and has no channel here yet. Reported as the *_assisted figures; the unassisted figures beside them exclude tutors entirely.

ENTERS-THE-BATTLEFIELD PAYOFFS are modelled: damage equal to the entering creature's power (Terror of the Peaks), X damage where X counts your board (Scourge of Valkas, Dragon Tempest), a token (Lathliss) and a token COPY of what entered (Miirym). Every arrival fires them — cast, token or copy — and a copy is itself an arrival, so they compound, which is the deck working rather than a bug. A payoff worded 'another NONTOKEN' does not re-trigger on its own tokens, which is the brake the rules already had. A chain is capped at 12 deep. X counts the whole board rather than one subtype: exact where the creatures are Dragons, generous otherwise.

The COMMANDER joins the battlefield when cast, attacks, and fires its own triggers. It used to be a mana sink and a flag — cast, then dropped — so a 10/10 flier contributed no power and never swung. Commander tax, death and recasting are still not modelled: it is cast once and it stays.

STATIC cost reduction IS modeled: a commander's eminence from the command zone (live from turn one, unremovable) and typed reducers once they are on the battlefield. It pays GENERIC only and is floored at the coloured pip count, because a discount can never pay a pip. A reduction that SCALES with a board state (Animar, Rakdos, Hamza) is refused rather than counted flat, and cost reduction on artifacts, noncreature spells or a colour is not modeled at all.

Extra card draw is NOT modeled: one card per turn, always. That understates every deck, but by an amount proportional to how much draw it runs — so it is conservative WITHIN a deck and not neutral BETWEEN them. `meta.card_advantage` reports how much of each list this hides. Card advantage is measured nowhere in this suite.

engine.thesis: A free, repeatable sacrifice outlet turns every body you control into three payments at once — a -1/-1 counter, a card, and one life off every seat — and the deck's real question is never how to go infinite but which of six kills the outlet is holding, because the three that ARE unbounded (stacks 009, 011, 012) need no commander and no counter, while the Nest of Scarabs line everyone names was measured by four passing stacks as a body-bounded rotation that grinds rather than wins.

diagnosis.verdict: The grind layer is genuinely well built: fodder and drain both at 82.3% drawn, outlets 78.5%, ignition 73.8%, turn-3 land drop 91.6%. The mana still functions after the reminder-text fix, but with a much thinner margin than the tracked diagnosis claimed — colour-sources is +2 over Karsten's target, not +5, which removes any land from the cut list and does NOT change what binds. What binds is unchanged: interaction-breadth at 2 of 5 classes, with artifact at zero by enumeration over all 80 entries, while this deck's own hosers (Grafdigger's Cage, Cursed Totem) are artifacts and three of six declared kills are commander-gated. The first table run adds one usable fact and one non-fact: the pod's clock is long (mean round 17.1, our seat eliminated at global turn 30.44), so the assisted assembly rates and not the by-turn-6 rates are the number that matters; and the 0.1 win rate is not a measurement, because Forge's own AI notes say it is 'pretty bad for most combo decks'.

open_questions.question: Does Ashnod's Altar + Pitiless Plunderer + Reassembling Skeleton hold as an unbounded line on a real board? Commander Spellbook rates it bracket 1 for infinite colorless mana and infinite death triggers, all three cards are in the 99, and the arithmetic looks self-funding (sacrifice for {C}{C} plus a Treasure, recur for {1}{B}), but nothing has resolved it and neither Plunderer nor the Skeleton appears in any of the eleven passing stacks.

Does Mikaeus, the Unhallowed plus ONE free sacrifice outlet loop without the commander? Seven such pairings are in candidate_lines (Carrion Feeder, Viscera Seer, Woe Strider, Yahenni, Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Blasting Station) and all seven outlets are in the 99, but undying's intervening 'if' fails the moment the body carries a +1/+1 counter — which is exactly what stack 010 needed Yawgmoth's -1/-1 counter to strip.

How many Nest of Scarabs rotations, across how many turns, does an average board actually need to kill a four-opponent pod? Stacks 002/003/004/005 each measure exactly ONE rotation from a three-body board — 5 to 8 activations, 7 to 13 drains, 28 to 52 life removed from 160 — and none of them carries the board into a second turn.

Against three opponents, is a nine-deep drain layer and an eight-deep outlet layer the right investment when the deck cannot answer an artifact at all? The two hosers that switch this deck off — Grafdigger's Cage on the graveyard casting and the undying returns, Cursed Totem on every creature outlet including the commander — are both artifacts, the artifact class is covered zero times, and Feed the Swarm reaches only creatures and enchantments.

Under an opposing Grafdigger's Cage, do KILL A (stack 009), KILL B (011), KILL D (010) and KILL F (014) still function? A and B recast Gravecrawler from the graveyard; D and F return creature cards to the battlefield from the graveyard via undying.

Under an opposing Cursed Totem, what survives of the outlet component? Five of its eight members are creatures whose ability is activated (Viscera Seer, Carrion Feeder, Woe Strider, Yahenni, Warren Soultrader) and Yawgmoth himself is shut off; three are artifacts (Ashnod's Altar, Phyrexian Altar, Blasting Station).

Does the corrected black-source count warrant a 37th land? The audit reads 38 sources against a target of 36; of the five nonland sources, Dark Ritual is one-shot and Pawn of Ulamog is credited only through mana_analysis's colour-identity fallback, since its sole mana clause is an Eldrazi Spawn token's 'Sacrifice this token: Add {C}'.
How often does the deck assemble ANY of its six kills? The audit states its schema cannot express the union, and averaging the six would invent a number the simulation never measured.

Should the fast-mana any_of group be re-curated — adding Culling the Weak if it lands, and deciding whether Jet Medallion belongs, since it accelerates Yawgmoth to an effective three mana but is cost reduction rather than mana?

Is Withering Torment worth a third slot alongside Gate to Phyrexia? The two are named as closers for the same single point of failure, and the deck's declared noncreature-answer group is one card (Feed the Swarm) at 17.1%. Re-curating that group to name the two or three real answers would give the question a measured rate to argue against instead of a count.

piloting.reading: our seat was handled about as well as the pod, so an A/B between two of your own lists against this table is played equally badly on both sides and remains informative. It is still not a claim about how the deck plays in your hands.

next: broken down for parts — the play/measure loop is closed for this deck (broken-down); its artifacts stay as published. Suggestions to log a game, simulate or run an experiment are withheld
